Police detained five men during a drug operation in Água Clara on 4 and 5
November 2026. Four were arrested on suspicion of drug trafficking and
association for trafficking, while the fifth was held on an outstanding warrant. The operation began after Military Police received a tip that a man was
selling drugs from a white VW Gol in Jardim das Palmeiras.

Officers pursued and stopped the driver, finding suspected cocaine in the car
and cannabis portions, a scale, packaging and cash at his home. The home
portions weighed about 20 grams, according to Rádio Caçula. Investigators
then identified another property used to store drugs, where police found 59
tablets weighing about 54 kilograms of cannabis and arrested two men.

Officers subsequently found another suspect with approximately 500 grams of
cannabis and a precision scale.

report.body:
Mossos d'Esquadra arrested seven men and seized 8,025 kilograms of hashish at an
industrial warehouse in Cabanes, Girona, on 1 October 2026. The men, aged
29 to 55, were suspected of links to a drug-trafficking organisation.
Investigators said they found the men unloading pallets from a trailer for
distribution into vans.

The hashish was hidden among merchandise in large raffia sacks filled with
shredded rubber, which investigators said made it harder to detect during
checks. Police found a firearm in one of the detained men's vans. The
seized hashish had an estimated illicit-market value of more than 16.2 million
euros.

The investigation began in June after Mossos intercepted a van carrying about
2,400 kilograms of hashish in Viladecans, Barcelona, and subsequently traced it
to the Cabanes warehouse. The seven detainees were brought before the court
in Figueres, and the investigation remained open.

report.title: Ceuta truck driver held in pretrial detention after hashish seizure
report.summary: A judge ordered a truck driver held in pretrial detention after UDYCO officers found bags of hashish hidden in his truck at Ceuta port. The weight remained unofficial and estimates differed.
report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. On 15 November, a judge ordered the driver held in pretrial detention over an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments.

report.title: Five arrested in Palma as police seize 60 kg of hashish
report.summary: National Police arrested four men and a woman during an investigation in Palma and seized 60 kilograms of hashish. Officers intercepted 24 kilograms in a package and found another 36 kilograms in a home.
report.body:
Spain's National Police arrested four men and one woman in Palma on suspicion of
belonging to a drug-trafficking group, and seized 60 kilograms of hashish.
The force's narcotics group said the investigation had begun months earlier. Officers intercepted a package addressed to a Palma resident and arrested
him after finding 24 kilograms of hashish inside.

Investigators identified other people they believed were collaborating and
searched two homes. At the principal suspect's home, police found 36
kilograms of hashish, an air rifle with a silencer and approximately €10,000 in
cash. They arrested a man and a woman there on suspicion of drug
trafficking and belonging to a criminal group or organisation. At the other
home, officers arrested a man suspected of guarding and transporting drugs and
found cocaine, a pistol, a bow and a hydraulic press.

Police arrested another person in connection with the case and suspected the
drugs were distributed to others for smaller-scale sales. The investigation
remained open and police did not rule out further arrests.

Police destroyed about 53,000 suspected cannabis plants at two farms at Yaruni
Bend, Linden, on 10 September 2026. No arrests were made, and police said
investigations were continuing.

The two farms covered about eight acres, or 3.24 hectares, and the plants ranged
from two to six feet tall. Officers found two makeshift camps and two
drying areas containing a combined 10 pounds (about 4.54 kilograms) of dried
cannabis. The plants, dried cannabis, camps and drying areas were destroyed
by fire. Police estimated the total value of the narcotics destroyed at
GY$22,038,728. The exercise was led by a gazetted officer and lasted from
5:30 a.m. to 4:36 p.m.

report.body:
Hong Kong Customs arrested a 24-year-old mainland Chinese man at Hong Kong
International Airport after finding suspected cannabis buds in his carry-on
baggage. He had arrived from Bangkok, Thailand, on the night of 4 November
2026 and was stopped during customs clearance in the early hours of 5 November. Customs said it seized about 9 kilograms of suspected cannabis buds, which
it estimated had a market value of about HK$1.9 million.

The man was charged with one count of trafficking in a dangerous drug and was
due before West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts on 6 November. Under the
Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, the maximum penalty for trafficking in a dangerous
drug is life imprisonment and a HK$5 million fine upon conviction. Customs
said it would continue to select passengers from high-risk regions for clearance
using risk assessment and to strengthen enforcement through intelligence
analysis.

a car travelling from Andhra Pradesh. They were Vasanthi and her sister's
daughter Shanmugapriya, both from the Kovilpatti area of Pudukkottai.

enforcement police. Officers found packets of cannabis concealed in bundles
in the car and seized the vehicle as well. Daily Thanthi put the estimated
value of the cannabis at about 13 lakh rupees (₹1.3 million).

A preliminary investigation alleged that the women planned to distribute the
cannabis to local agents in Pudukkottai and surrounding areas. Police
registered a case and investigated who drove the car and who else might be
involved. Dinamani reported that the women were jailed after their arrests.

No plea or final court outcome was reported.
The cannabis product was not specified.
report.body:
Saratoga County sheriff's deputies arrested Kevin C. Wilbur and Quinton L. Carle
after a traffic stop on the Northway in Clifton Park. The sheriff's office
said deputies seized 489 pounds (about 221.8 kilograms) of cannabis. Each
man was charged with first-degree criminal possession of cannabis.

Deputies said the vehicle was stopped at 2:28 p.m. for following too closely and
insufficient tail lamps, and Wilbur was cited for both traffic violations.
Both men were arraigned in Clifton Park Town Court before Judge Jennifer Jeram. Wilbur was remanded to the Saratoga County Jail, while Carle was released
on his own recognizance pending further proceedings.

report.body:
Kern County deputies arrested Rogelio Lorenzo Francisca, 32, of Guerrero,
Mexico, after a cannabis search near Taft, California. He was arrested on
suspicion of marijuana cultivation, marijuana for sale, conspiracy and delaying,
resisting or obstructing arrest, and booked into the Taft jail facility.

On 8 October 2026, Taft substation deputies executed a search warrant in the
27000 block of Highway 119 with the sheriff’s High Intensity Drug Trafficking
Areas Task Force and Taft police. The sheriff’s office said officers
eradicated 660 marijuana plants during the search. Authorities also
reported finding dangerous pesticides at the grow site. The sheriff’s
office said the investigation remained active.
